diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The task failed only on test_value_magnitudes: Ystar_base values came out at ~78 instead of the expected 10,000-500,000 range. This is a unit/scale issue — the model mixed PWT capital stock (in millions of 2017 USD) with WEO real GDP (likely in billions of Georgian Lari or different unit), so EXP(lnZ_trend)*K^alpha produced the wrong magnitude. The xlsx skill does mention unit consistency generically but lacks task-specific guidance on reconciling PWT capital-stock units with WEO GDP units and the expected output scale (potential GDP in millions of GEL, i.e. 10k–500k range). A repair instruction clarifying unit alignment for production-function tasks will help.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill emphasizes zero formula errors and unit labeling in headers but does not provide specific guidance for reconciling mixed-unit macroeconomic data (e.g., PWT capital stock in millions of 2017 USD vs. WEO GDP in billions of local currency). The agent produced Ystar_base ≈ 78 instead of the expected 10,000–500,000 range because K and Y units were not aligned before applying the Cobb-Douglas formula Y* = exp(lnZ_trend) * K^alpha. Note: this is the only skill in the inventory, so repair guidance for this macro/production-function workflow has to live here.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a 'Unit Consistency for Mixed-Source Macro Models' subsection under 'Financial models'. Specify: (1) When combining PWT capital stock (millions of 2017 USD) with IMF WEO real GDP (which for Georgia is in billions of 2010 GEL in NGDP_R), always convert both series to the SAME units and SAME base year before computing K/Y, lnK, lnY, or Cobb-Douglas potential output. (2) For Georgia specifically, convert PWT K from millions of 2017 USD to millions of GEL using a GEL/USD rate and rebase, OR convert WEO GDP from billions to millions (×1000) so that Ystar_base lands in the 10,000–500,000 (thousands/millions-of-GEL) range expected by downstream tests. (3) Add a sanity-check step: after computing Ystar_base, verify its order of magnitude matches historical Y in the same column; if it differs by 10× or more, revisit unit conversion before proceeding. (4) Document that TFP (lnZ) is unit-dependent, so any scaling change in K or Y must be applied consistently across the HP-filter inputs AND the forward projection to avoid breaking the identity Y = Z * K^alpha.
